harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1's kernel to boot with audit=1 persistently via grubby (updated all BLS boot entries and /etc/default/grub), then rebooted the node and verified the boot identity changed and audit=1 is active in the live kernel.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: boot_id bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a, /proc/cmdline without audit=1, auditd active (cmd-42cae116a589443e, cmd-9fbdaebb8c7445d6)
Ran `sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1` to persist audit=1 into all BLS boot entries (cmd-7091b2fa56ff4d1d)
Rebooted node1 via `sudo systemctl reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect (cmd-c60a8c44302e401d)
Polled node1 until it responded again after reboot (cmd-8b677b96206b4811)
Verified new boot_id 648ac338-ec58-49ff-a65c-eecbaf04c191, /proc/cmdline contains audit=1, auditd active, auditctl -s shows enabled 1 (cmd-5142229989014505)

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before change (boot identity, auditd status)
evidence.summary: Captured original boot_id bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a, original /proc/cmdline (no audit=1), and auditd active before making changes.

evidence.requirement: Kernel boot parameter audit=1 persisted across reboots (config-level)
evidence.summary: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1 added audit=1 to both BLS entries (normal + rescue), and /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX also updated to include audit=1.

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background so the exec call returned/acknowledged before the connection dropped due to the restart.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Node became reachable again after polling, and boot_id changed from bef0e5ec-ce32-423b-826a-8a5a90584d3a to 648ac338-ec58-49ff-a65c-eecbaf04c191, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: audit=1 actually took effect in the running kernel post-reboot
evidence.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows audit=1, auditd service is active, and auditctl -s reports 'enabled 1', confirming the kernel booted with auditing enabled and the setting is live.

attempts.summary: Configured node1's kernel to boot with audit=1 persistently via grubby (updated all BLS boot entries and /etc/default/grub), then rebooted the node and verified the boot identity changed and audit=1 is active in the live kernel.
